name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(3,4),(0,2),$ and $(7,10).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(0,1)$
- $(2,3)$
- $(1,0)$
worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${S}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,1),(-1,2),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

EXPLANATION

First, we create a matrix Y containing all of the vertices of S′:

Y=[3074210]

Now, if X denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of S, we have

T⋅X=YT⋅X=[3074210].

We need to reverse the action of the matrix T. So, we multiply the above equation by T−1, and we get

T−1⋅T⋅X=T−1⋅[3074210]X=T−1⋅[3074210].

The inverse of T is T−1=14−2[2−1−22]=12[2−1−22].

Therefore, we obtain X=T−1⋅[3074210]=12[2−1−22][3074210]=[1−12123].

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are (1,1),(−1,2),(2,3).

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
